summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and a history of gastritis was re-admitted for worsening epigastric abdominal pain and nausea shortly after discharge from a prior admission for similar symptoms. Initial evaluation ruled out cardiac ischemia and acute cholecystitis. A targeted ultrasound showed no hernia or granuloma near the pacemaker site. The patient was kept NPO initially, then advanced to liquids and regular diet as symptoms improved. Aspirin was reduced from 325 mg to 81 mg daily to minimize gastric irritation. He underwent hemodialysis without complications and was discharged home in stable condition with continued twice-daily Nexium and GI follow-up.
